summary: 1. The 25-Aug-24-Sep fiscal production month closed on Sep 24 at +6.02% on total BCM, but the crusher closed the same cycle at just 38.75% of plan. 2. Total BCM landed at 634,663 against a 598,598 BCM target, with the day itself essentially flat against its own daily target (+0.02%) and ore recovering off Sep 23's complete zero-ore day (though still -40.55% against its own daily target). 2. 3. Crusher stockpile-to-crusher throughput closed the month at 48,055.5 LCM against the 124,000 LCM plan, the widest shortfall of any KPI this article tracks this cycle, driven by roughly 5h47m of crusher downtime on the closing day alone (bin-level-low, big boulders, and a 4h42m "crusher bin chowk" stop). 3. 4. On the fleet side, DT-107 opened a fresh Engine Coolant Temperature High fault, the same fault type already open on DT-128 (now its seventh day down), while Track Dozer DZ-248's Track Completely Worn-out fault, first logged the day before, cleared the same morning it opened, and EX-253 and EX-123 extended their own standing stoppages to nine and three days down respectively. 5. See [[daily-production-report]] and [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. 6. DT-107's new engine-coolant fault is the pass's clearest watch item. 7. It opened at 3:30 AM on Sep 24 and stayed down the full 24 hours with no repair movement visible by report cutoff, mirroring DT-128's own still-open, multi-day version of the identical fault type. 8. See [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. 9. New longer-duration ancillary-fleet faults opened on WL-295 and WL-329 (Filter Cleaning/Daily Check/Adaptor Missing on WL-295; Fuel Tank Cracked plus Cutting Edge Replacement on WL-329, spanning into the next day) — both worth a repair-timeline check on the next pass. See [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. Sep 24's own survey reconciliation, which would close the fiscal month on the survey side, has not landed yet — the standing file-N-reports-day-(N-1) publishing lag means it is due on the next survey workbook. [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] still reflects Sep 23 (93.39% of the monthly target, one day left at that point). Worth checking on the next pass whether the survey-side close-out lands near the trucks-reported +6.02%, or below 100% the way every prior month has closed. New October forward-planning material landed but was not compiled this pass: an October 2026 monthly production/availability forecast and a Week 39+40 two-week forecast workbook, both registered for provenance and flagged for a future dedicated forecast-compile pass, consistent with this pass's dashboard-scoped time budget.
